name: Eleazar
overview: Eleazar was a male figure consecrated to keep the ark of God in Kiriath-jearim, as recorded in 1 Samuel 7:1. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes provided for him. His role highlights a sacred responsibility related to the custody of the ark during a significant period in Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Eleazar means 'G-d [El] is a help,' reflecting a divine assistance theme inherent in his identity. This proper name, mentioned in 1 Samuel 7:1, emphasizes reliance on God's support and aid.
familyAndRelationships: Eleazar is identified as the son of Abinadab according to the explicit relationship noted in 1 Samuel 7:1. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Eleazar's significance lies in his consecration to guard the ark of God at Kiriath-jearim, a role that underscores the reverence and care given to the sacred presence of God among His people. This responsibility situates Eleazar within the narrative of Israel's spiritual history, marking him as a key caretaker of the ark during a transitional phase for the nation. His service reflects the importance of faithful stewardship in preserving God's holiness.
